He gave one example — Daytona written as a nothing burger when USD 200 of its credit runs a
full VM for a month with no card — and asked for ten free tiers, ten beefy paid and ten
micro paid, each with a direct cart link. The method that found the errors was not a re-read of the pages. It was **following the
vendor's own "Order now" href and reading what the cart charged**. That single step
contradicted four published recommendations.

## The four corrections

**1. VolpaByte Ryzen KVM 8 GB is dead, and it was the top recommendation.**

Its marketing page still renders "Ryzen KVM 8 GB EUR 4,99 pro Monat", 6 AMD Ryzen vCores and
8 GB DDR4-3200 ECC. Its own "Jetzt bestellen" href is
`dashboard/index.php?rp=/store/vps/ryzen-kvm-8-gb`, which redirects to `/store` and renders:

> Could not load any product groups. The plan cannot be bought at the advertised price. `verdict` moved from
`qualifies-with-caveat` to **`dead`**. This was independently observed by lane N07 and
re-read by the parent session.

**2. The order page says **2 vCore** and **USD 5.50 a month
or USD 55.00 a year**. USD 4.58 is the annual rate divided by twelve, so the row is still
under the line on annual prepay, but the monthly list is over it and the shape was wrong by
a factor of four. Separately, HostBrr's marketing "Deploy Server" button points at
`pricing_id=1166` and renders `Subtotal: $0.00 USD ... Total Due Today: $0.00 USD`; the
working link is the group page.

**3. DediRock is both a fossil and a live offer, at two different URLs.**

The Black Friday page advertises a USD 9.88/year Saver. Its Order href
`…/store/promo-vp/promo-vps-saver-ny-bf` lands on a category listing whose cheapest line is
**USD 5.99 per month** for a different shape — no error, no sold-out marker. That is a
fossil, and it is what the corpus had recorded. But the standing promo SKU at `…/store/promo-vp/promo-vps-special-ny` is a different
product and it **does** sell. The operator cleared the Cloudflare challenge and the rendered
order form was read directly: **2 GiB / 1 vCPU / 30 GB / 2 TB / 1 IPv4, "Annually: $9.88
USD", "$9.88 USD Total Due Today"**. So the earlier verdict was right about the URL it checked and wrong as a statement about the
host. The corpus had no record for the SKU that works.

**4. The USD 50 card hold does not exist anywhere in this corpus.**

The largest hold found remains Koyeb at USD 29. The typical is USD 1. Oracle's is USD 1.00. it is not what these
records show, and the page now says so with the numbers.

## What the cart audit found across 42 rows

Lane N07 followed the order link on every qualifying row at or under USD 5 and read the
destination:

| verdict | n | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cart prices the plan | 16 | link is good |
| cart prices something else, is out of stock, or is walled | 14 | link is bad |
| no price readable by GET | 12 | JS shell, `action=add`, or no SKU |

**Nine were fossils of the DediRock class** — the link resolves to a different product or to
nothing: `luo-cloud-lxc-nat` (CNY 1.50 advertised, CNY 25.00 category rendered, 16.7×),
`natkvm-nat-lxc`, `dedirock` ×2, `softshellweb-lxc-ipv6-only`, `volpabyte-ryzen-kvm-8gb`,
`62yun-promo-vds`, `firstbyte-msk-kvm-start`, `alibaba-swas-intl`. Three were **out of stock but correctly linked** — a stock fact, not a broken link:
`vds6-v6-1`, `greencloud-budget-kvm-8gb`, `cloudfanatic-standard-1gb`.

## What replaced them

**Q1 beefy:** **AlphaVPS C6G** returns as the pick, at EUR 50.90 a year for 3 vCPU / 6 GiB /
55 GB NVMe / 6 TB / 1 IPv4 + a /64. It is the only row where a real browser read the cart,
it priced exactly as advertised, and it is in stock. ⚠ **Two of seven locations only** —
Sofia and Los Angeles; London, Nuremberg, Dallas, New York and Seattle render "Out of
stock".

**Best value per gigabyte:** **HostBrr ECO 4 GB** at USD 32.50 a year (USD 2.71/mo), cart
prices it exactly.

**Q2 micro:** **DediRock Promo Special NY at USD 0.82** is now the WireGuard pick and the
only sub-dollar row with a **dedicated IPv4** and **2 GiB** — four times the next-largest
machine in the band. **TierHive at USD 0.10** stays the monitor.

**Free tiers:** the ten are reordered around the card column. **Daytona moves from sixth to
fourth** with the arithmetic the operator supplied: USD 200 is 749 hours of a 4 vCPU / 4 GiB
VM, 31.2 days, no card. Twelve rows are `unknown` on the cart because settling them needs a browser session or an
  account.
- **Hostodo's Black Friday 2025 remains unverified.** A control request with a bogus plan
  code returned **byte-identical** output, so its HTTP 200 proves nothing.
- **DediRock's renewal is not published.** USD 9.88 is year one; year two is unknown.
- **Datalix's cart arrived logged in as another person** (`Eingeloggt als
  [address removed]`), so its `cart_works` is weaker than the other rows.

## A correction to this correction: VolpaByte is not dead

This entry first recorded VolpaByte as `dead`, on the strength of nine order links that each
rendered **"Could not load any product groups."** That verdict was wrong, and the way it was
wrong matters more than the verdict did.

**A stateless fetch makes a healthy WHMCS store look dead.** Lane N04 found it: carry a
cookie jar from `volpabyte.net/` first, and the identical URL redirects to
`cart.php?a=confproduct&i=0` and prints all four billing cycles. The parent session then ran
the control both ways:

| request | final URL | body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no cookie jar (what the broker does) | `…/dashboard/index.php?rp=/store` | **"Could not load any product groups"**, zero prices |
| jar warmed from the homepage | `…/dashboard/cart.php?a=confproduct&i=0` | **EUR 4,99 / 14,22 / 26,95 / 50,90**, full configurator |

Same URL, same minute, opposite answers. The vendor never changed anything. The cart prints four cycles and says nothing about year
two; EUR 4.99 monthly is the only evidence for month 13, and that is an inference.

### The guard this produced

A note would not have stopped this, because three independent readers hit it in one session. `scripts/probe/cartcheck.py` now does the read with a jar and exits `0` only when the cart
priced something. It was tested both ways before being documented: `priced` and exit 0 on
VolpaByte, `error` and exit 1 on the DediRock fossil, `no-price` and exit 1 on a page with no
cart. Withdrawn as unverified. The honest statement is USD 3.75 now and month 13
  unknown.
- **TierHive's "USD 0.10 with a cart"** — no cart exists. Every Deploy button, Micro
  included, points at `control.tierhive.com/register`, which redirects to `/login`. Each one changed a
record.

### 1. Cheap-Host's plan table is read, and its top rung is the biggest NAT machine found

`cheap-host.onl/nat-vps/?lang=en` renders **four** rungs, not the one the corpus carried:

| rung | RUB/mo | USD/mo | vCPU | RAM | NVMe |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NAT Start | 59 | 0.73 | 1 | 1 GB | 10 GB |
| NAT Base | 99 | 1.22 | 1 | 2 GB | 15 GB |
| NAT Pro | 199 | **2.45** | 2 | **4 GB** | 25 GB |
| NAT Plus | 349 | 4.29 | 4 | **8 GB** | 50 GB |

All four: unlimited traffic, 100 Mbit/s, Germany, shared IPv4 with **no IPv6**,
**999 TCP/UDP ports + SSH**, **port 25 blocked**. Both are now
settled from the plan card. **NAT Pro at USD 2.45 for 4 GB and 2 vCPU is more machine than
any other NAT row in the corpus under USD 3**, and 999 forwarded ports is the widest block
found anywhere. Two things still keep it out of the ranked ten: every "Choose plan" button routes to the
account panel, so **no price renders before login** (`cart_works: unknown`), and its rails
are SBP, SberPay, YooMoney, MIR and crypto — **no card-network rail**.

### 2. VolpaByte charges 19% VAT, and the corpus said it did not

The order summary reads `Monthly: €4,19 EUR`, `VAT @ 19.00%: €0,80 EUR`, `€4,99 EUR Total Due
Today`. So **EUR 4.99 is gross and EUR 4.19 is net**, and there is no country selector to make
the VAT fall away for a non-EU buyer. This record had said "no VAT line and no country selector". The second half was right and the
first was wrong. RackNerd's Black Friday 2025 is confirmed out of stock at the product URL itself

`my.racknerd.com/index.php?rp=store/blackfriday2025/1-gb-kvm-vps-black-friday-2025` renders:

> Oops, there's a problem… **Out of Stock** — The plan you selected is out of stock and not
> available for ordering at this time. Previously this rested on a `0 Available` counter elsewhere in the store. It now rests on the
product page refusing the plan, which is the stronger form of the same finding.

### 4. Hostodo stays unverified, and now for a stated reason

The deploy console loads but prints no price, and a control request with a bogus plan code
returned byte-identical output. Reading the price needs a signed-in session, and this corpus
creates no accounts. however, your card will not be charged. So the gate is: **no card for most new customers**, and a **USD 1 hold for 3–5 days** when one
is asked for. The machine is a `t4g.small` — 2 vCPU, 2 GiB of Graviton — free for **750 hours
a month**, plus USD 100 of credits on signup and up to USD 100 more.

⛔ **The end is hard:** *"Your free account plan ends after six months or when your credits are
fully used — whichever occurs first. After your free account plan expires, your account closes
automatically."* That is a six-month stop, not a renewal, and AWS retains content for 90 days. AWS enters the free-tier ten at **fourth**, displacing Waifly to eleventh.

### Oracle's USD 1.00 hold is withdrawn

Oracle's signup page states that a hold exists and **publishes no amount**. The USD 1.00 figure

**453 compute records carried `identity_cost.detail: "as stated by the provider's signup page"`**

## The defect class that keeps recurring

⭐ **Four more hiding negatives were found and corrected in `micro.md` alone**, where the
document asserted:

- "No verified full VPS exists below USD 1.42" — **12 documented records** sit between USD 0.10
  and USD 0.90.
- "No record names a passport or residence document" — **26 compute records** carry
  `identity_kind: national-id`.
- "`hetzner-dedicated` carries no shape and no price" — its notes price the AX41 at EUR 59.00.
- "Four things would put a row under it" — all four had already happened. That is now **seven** hiding negatives in this topic. Every one was a claim about absence written
without a search that could have found the counterexample. **A negative is a claim about a
search, and it carries the search's scope in the same sentence or it is not a finding.**

## What the document audits found

Four documents audited for the first time, 300+ claims checked:

- **`lowend-vps.md` had the market's shape backwards**: it claimed three rows under USD 2 and
  said every one is IPv6-only or NAT. There are **19**, and 8 carry an IPv4. The real shared
  constraint is prepay: 15 of the 19 price only a six-month or longer term.
- **`vps-monthly.md` crowned a box nobody can buy**: the Hetzner CX23 is marked "not available"
  on every rung of its line. The answer is now Contabo's Cloud VPS 4 at USD 6.60.
- **`cloud-vms.md`: 14 of 35 table rows disagreed with the record they cite**, all drift since
  the last rewrite. Five monthly figures elsewhere were the 10-hour column quoted as a monthly
  bill.
- **`always-on-free.md`'s tier table was fiction** in five places, including GitHub Codespaces
  filed DEAD when its record says `qualifies`.
- **`micro.md` applied Modal's list rate to a Sandbox** in four places; the page prints
  "Sandboxes are billed at non-preemptible rates of 3x list price", so a minimum container is
  USD 0.0207/h and USD 30 buys 1,446 Sandbox hours, not 4,348.

## The two niche catalogues, audited last

`forum-hosts.md` and `regional-clouds.md` were the last two documents in this topic never checked.
**133 claims checked, 25 failed.** The corrections that matter:

- **`sanfengyun` was mis-kinded.** Its record said `email` while its own offer text says a mobile
  number plus a CNY 0.3 real-name certification. Now `national-id`, which is the gate the
  operator cannot pass.
- **`cloudcone` prices were recorded as unpublished** when the record carries USD 28, 46 and 69
  a year for its three rungs.
- **`iwinv`'s monthly cap was arithmetic that did not hold**: 30 x KRW 210 = 6,300 against a
  5,600 monthly ceiling. A false finding, correctly retracted rather than kept.
- **`chataoyun` was a typo** for `chamaoyun`.

⚠ **A count C3 measured mid-pass went stale before it landed.** It reported 450 records naming a
gate without pricing it, against the pre-repair dossier. The repair merged afterwards, so the
figure is now 266. Corrected in place with the sequence stated, along with five other `1,239`
counts that the merge to 1,255 had outdated.

`https://boat.dev/`: "Billed per second, free when stopped. 7-day free trial, then from

`https://boat.dev/compare`: "25 free hours to start". The `/free-trial` page that the documentation links to returns 404, so the trial's allowance
cannot be established from the vendor. Only the clock can.

## What it changes

The verdict becomes `trial-only`, the identity cost becomes `card`, and the binding
constraint becomes the trial clock plus the 14-day stopped-disk window, which is the term
that actually destroys work: a stopped sandbox keeps its disk for 14 days and is then
deleted without recovery. The comparison page also carries the reason this record was opened at all: it lists
fourteen sandbox providers at one shape with list prices dated 2026-09-26, which is a
cross-check the corpus had never used.

`https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners`, read 2026-10-22,
states "Use of the standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited on public
repositories". The billing page says the same in different words and adds the sentence that
matters for GPU work: "Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public
repositories".

## What it changes

The verdict becomes `qualifies-with-caveat`, and the binding constraint moves to the job cap:
6 hours per job, 20 concurrent jobs on the Free plan. A job killed at 6 hours cannot use the
rest of an unlimited allowance, so the cap is what decides the shape of a workload. GPU runners are not free on any plan. They are larger runners, billed per minute, and sold to
Team and Enterprise. A reader who reads "unlimited" and plans a GPU job has misread it.
